### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the elapsed time between consecutive completion events for every observed pair (A03,A09), (A04,A09), (A05,A09), (A06,A09), (A07,A09) and (A08,A09) sat around 1 hour (means 0.98–1.02 h, medians about 0.95–1.02 h). In the later window, the same elapsed times sat around 2 hours (means 1.92–2.04 h, medians about 1.89–2.03 h) — an increase of roughly 0.9–1.1 hours, i.e. the intervals roughly doubled. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003, TWAIT004, TWAIT005, TWAIT006]
- The shift moves the whole distribution, not only the average: for example, the middle half of the (A03,A09) intervals went from about 0.88–1.06 hours to about 1.82–2.16 hours, and the spread widened modestly across all pairs (standard deviations from about 0.14–0.20 hours to about 0.24–0.37 hours). [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003, TWAIT004, TWAIT005, TWAIT006]
- Each of the six differences is larger than in about 999.5 of 1000 random re-splits of the pooled data (2000 reference comparisons each). The time family produced 6 qualifying items where roughly 0.008 were expected if nothing had changed, while no control-flow item qualified (0 against about 0.23 expected). [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003, TWAIT004, TWAIT005, TWAIT006, screening]
- How often each pair was observed changed only modestly and in mixed directions (for instance (A04,A09) fell from 40 to 30 intervals, (A05,A09) rose from 35 to 43, (A08,A09) stayed at 29), so the dominant difference lies in the elapsed times, not in how often these transitions occur. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003, TWAIT004, TWAIT005, TWAIT006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a timing change centred on A09 as a possibility: in the later window, the elapsed time between consecutive completion events on the transitions from each of A03, A04, A05, A06, A07 and A08 into A09 roughly doubled, from about 1 hour to about 2 hours. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003, TWAIT004, TWAIT005, TWAIT006]

The hypothesis rests on direct and consistent timing evidence: all six pairs into A09 show the same direction and a similar magnitude (about +0.9 to +1.1 hours), each is based on 29–43 observed intervals per window, each difference exceeds essentially all random re-splits, and 6 time items against an expectation of about 0.008 cannot be explained by chance as a whole. The absence of control-flow items (0 against about 0.23 expected) means no structural reorganisation passed the thresholds, which fits a pure timing change. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003, TWAIT004, TWAIT005, TWAIT006, screening]

Limitation: T_WAIT measures elapsed time between consecutive completion events, so the extra hour cannot be localised — it could reflect longer execution of the A03–A08 steps, a longer gap before A09 completes, or both. A competing explanation the evidence cannot fully exclude is a small structural insertion or reordering around A09 that stays below the control-flow thresholds. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003, TWAIT004, TWAIT005, TWAIT006, screening]

Other differences: only minor, mixed shifts in how often the pairs were observed (e.g. (A04,A09) from 40 to 30 intervals, (A05,A09) from 35 to 43), consistent with sampling variation between the windows rather than a participation change. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003, TWAIT004, TWAIT005, TWAIT006]
